author: Keystone Today
title: Olwethu Makhanya selected for South Africa's 2026 FIFA World Cup roster
text:
Philadelphia Union defender Olwethu Makhanya has been named to the final roster for South Africa’s national team at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Bafana Bafana head coach Hugo Broos announced on May 27. This selection comes as South Africa returns to the tournament for the first time since hosting in 2010.
Makhanya’s inclusion marks a significant moment for both his club and country. The 2026 tournament will be Bafana Bafana’s fourth appearance at a FIFA World Cup, following previous entries in 1998, 2002, and 2010. South Africa secured qualification with a decisive 3-0 victory over Rwanda, finishing atop Group C ahead of Nigeria.
South Africa has been placed in Group A alongside co-hosts Mexico, Republic of Korea, and Czechia. The team will begin its campaign against Mexico on June 11 at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City. Subsequent group matches are scheduled against Czechia on June 18 in Atlanta and Republic of Korea on June 24 in Monterrey.
Ahead of the tournament, South Africa is set to play a send-off match against Nicaragua on May 29 at Orlando Stadium as part of its preparations. At age twenty-two, Makhanya could become one of the first active Philadelphia Union players to participate in a FIFA World Cup match. He joins midfielder Danley Jean Jacques as a current Union member named to his national team’s final roster for this year’s competition.
Philadelphia Union features a roster of professional players competing in Major League Soccer and operates out of Subaru Park with dedicated training facilities; it also achieved the Supporters’ Shield in 2020 and maintains various community programs and youth initiatives, according to the official website .
